mainTopic: סנחריב's insult, his campaign against ירושלים, and how חזקיה's תורה-learning generation was saved
overview: This amud is all about סנחריב, the king of Assyria who attacked ירושלים in the days of חזקיה. It starts by finishing a rule from the previous daf: פרעה insulted God himself and was punished by God Himself, while סנחריב insulted God through messengers and was punished through a messenger, an angel. The גמרא explains סנחריב's boast to destroy God's dwelling below and above. It also explains why his messenger רבשקה claimed God had sent him: he had heard ישעיהו's prophecy about the king of Assyria. The גמרא then asks why סנחריב was punished, and answers that he went beyond the prophecy by aiming at ירושלים, a city protected by its people's hard work in תורה. Next it praises חזקיה's generation, where even children knew the laws of טומאה and טהרה, and explains that God swore ahead of time to hand סנחריב's army over as spoils. The prophet tells the people that each may keep the spoils he takes, even Jewish property the enemy had captured. Finally, רב הונא says סנחריב marched ten stages in one day, and the גמרא begins explaining the place names in the פסוק, an explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Punished through a messenger, just as he insulted through a messenger
steps.stepSummary: The end of the rule: someone who insulted God through a messenger is punished by God through a messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who insulted God] through a messenger, God punished him through a messenger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started on the previous daf. The rule is that God punishes a person in the same way the person insulted Him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full rule has two halves. If someone insults God personally, God punishes him personally. If he insults God through a messenger, God punishes him through a messenger, and this line is that second half.

keyTerms.meaning: by means of a messenger or agent
The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)

phrases.english: by means of a messenger,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous daf: someone who insulted God through a messenger.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, exacted payment from him
by means of a messenger.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ, נִפְרַע הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the principle begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's punishment matches how the person insulted Him: through a messenger brings punishment through a messenger.

steps.title: Pharaoh insulted God himself and God punished him Himself
steps.stepSummary: פרעה spoke against God personally, so God personally drowned Egypt in the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: פרעה said, 'Who is God that I should listen to Him?' So God Himself punished him, as it says, 'God shook Egypt into the sea,' and 'You trod through the sea with Your horses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first example of the rule. פרעה insulted God with his own mouth, and God Himself punished him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרעה's words ('Who is ה׳') came straight from him, with no messenger in between. The verses say that God Himself overturned Egypt and rode with 'Your horses' through the sea, which shows the punishment came from God directly.

keyTerms.meaning: the king of Egypt in the time of משה
and He shook off or overturned

phrases.english: Pharaoh, about whom it is written:
"Who is the Lord that I should listen to His voice?"

phrases.aramaic: נִפְרַע הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ בְּעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, exacted payment from him Himself,
as it is written: "And the Lord shook Egypt
into the midst of the sea,"
and it is written: "You trod through the sea with Your horses, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the first half of the rule (personal insult, personal punishment).
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who insults God personally is punished by God personally.

steps.title: Sennacherib insulted God through messengers and was punished through an angel
steps.stepSummary: סנחריב insulted God through his messengers, so God punished him through an angel who struck his camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: About סנחריב it says, 'Through your messengers you insulted God.' So God punished him through a messenger, as it says, 'An angel of God went out and struck 185,000 in the Assyrian camp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second example. סנחריב sent messengers to insult God, so God sent a messenger, an angel, to punish him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'by the hand of your messengers' you insulted God, so the insult came through others. The punishment matches this: God did not strike the camp directly but sent 'an angel of ה׳.' In Hebrew the word מלאך means both 'messenger' and 'angel,' and that ties the two verses together.

keyTerms.meaning: the king of Assyria who attacked Jerusalem

steps.whatToRemember: פרעה insulted God himself and was punished by God Himself. סנחריב insulted God through messengers and was punished through a messenger (an angel). The punishment matches the sin.

phrases.english: Sennacherib, as it is written:
"By the hand of your messengers you have taunted the Lord,"
the Holy One, Blessed be He, exacted payment from him
by means of a messenger,
as it is written: "And the angel of the Lord went out
and struck in the camp of Assyria
one hundred eighty-five thousand, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the second half of the rule, as a parallel to the פרעה example.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who insults God through a messenger is punished through a messenger.

steps.title: Two verses describe Sennacherib's boast differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא points out that one verse says 'its farthest height' and the parallel verse says 'its farthest lodge.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא pointed out a contradiction: one verse says 'מרום קצו' (its farthest height), and another says 'מלון קצו' (its farthest lodging place).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a problem. Two verses that tell the same boast of סנחריב use different words, and the next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו and מלכים ב record the same speech, but one says 'height' (מרום) and the other says 'lodge' (מלון). If both are describing the same boast, why do the words differ? The question sets up an explanation of what סנחריב really planned.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa raised a contradiction:
It is written: "its farthest height,"
and it is written: "its farthest lodge."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues discussing סנחריב with a new question about his words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two parallel verses describing סנחריב's boast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same speech is quoted with two different words (מרום and מלון), which looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: He planned to destroy the dwelling below and then the dwelling above
steps.stepSummary: Both verses are true: סנחריב planned first to destroy the בית המקדש below and then to attack God's dwelling above.
steps.simpleTranslation: That wicked man said: 'First I will destroy the dwelling place below, and afterwards I will destroy the dwelling place above.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. Each verse describes a different part of סנחריב's plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lodge' (מלון) refers to the earthly dwelling, the בית המקדש. 'Height' (מרום) refers to the heavenly dwelling. סנחריב boasted that he would destroy both, one after the other, so the two verses do not contradict each other. Each one records a different stage of his plan.

phrases.english: That wicked one said:
First I will destroy the dwelling below,
phrases.notes: This matches 'its farthest lodge,' meaning the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אַחְרִיב דִּירָה שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
phrases.english: and afterward I will destroy the dwelling above.
phrases.notes: This matches 'its farthest height,' meaning God's place in heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each verse refers to a different object (two stages of one plan).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses seem to record the same boast with conflicting words.
steps.terutzMaskana: מלון is the earthly בית המקדש and מרום is the heavenly dwelling. סנחריב intended to destroy both.

steps.title: What did Rabshakeh mean by 'God told me to destroy this land'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks what רבשקה meant when he claimed that God had told him to go up and destroy the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is the meaning of the verse, 'Have I now come up against this place to destroy it without God? God said to me: Go up against this land and destroy it'? What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about a verse. רבשקה, סנחריב's messenger, claimed that God had sent him, and the גמרא asks what he was basing this on. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It sounds strange for an enemy general to claim that God had told him to attack Israel. The question 'מאי היא' asks what specific 'command' he was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written
what is it? (what does this refer to?)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Now, is it without the Lord that I have come up
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 18:25. These are the words of רבשקה, סנחריב's messenger.

phrases.english: against this place to destroy it?
The Lord said to me:
Go up against this land and destroy it."
What is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement about סנחריב's campaign, now focusing on his messenger's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What divine 'command' רבשקה was referring to when he said God told him to destroy the land.

steps.title: He had heard Isaiah's prophecy
steps.stepSummary: רבשקה based his claim on a prophecy of ישעיהו, which said that because the people rejected the waters of שילוח, God would bring the king of Assyria against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had heard the prophet saying: 'Because this people rejected the gently flowing waters of שילוח, and rejoiced with רצין and the son of רמליהו...' (and the prophecy goes on to say God will bring the king of Assyria upon them).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבשקה was relying on a real prophecy he had heard from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו 8:6-7 says that because the people rejected the waters of שילוח and rejoiced with רצין and בן רמליהו, God would bring the king of Assyria against them. רבשקה took this as God's 'command' to attack. Here the גמרא quotes only the first half of the prophecy. After two side teachings it finishes the quote in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: the waters of the Shiloach spring in Jerusalem
רצין king of Aram and פקח son of רמליהו, king of the northern kingdom of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted verse does not mention Assyria at all. The point is in the next verse (ישעיהו 8:7), 'God brings upon them... the king of Assyria.' The גמרא quotes that verse a little later, in step 10.

phrases.english: That he heard the prophet who was saying:
"Because this people has rejected
the waters of Shiloah that flow slowly
and rejoices with Rezin and the son of Remaliah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבשקה relied on ישעיהו's prophecy (ישעיהו 8:6-7) that God would bring Assyria against the people for rejecting the waters of שילוח.

steps.title: The Aramaic translation explains the verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he understands the verse about the waters of שילוח only through its Aramaic תרגום. It says the people rejected the gentle rule of בית דוד and preferred רצין and בן רמליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If not for the Aramaic translation of this verse, I would not understand it. The translation says: Because this people hated the kingdom of בית דוד, which led them gently like the gently flowing waters of שילוח, and they preferred רצין and בן רמליהו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the hard verse from ישעיהו that was quoted in step 7, using its Aramaic translation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hebrew verse speaks in a picture: the people 'rejected the waters of שילוח.' The תרגום explains the picture. The quiet waters stand for the gentle kingdom of בית דוד, and the people chose the northern kings instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The Aramaic translation of the Tanach
The waters of the Shiloach spring, which flow gently
The son of Remalyahu, meaning פקח, king of the northern kingdom

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Were it not for the Aramaic translation of this verse,
I would not know what it is saying.
"Because this people loathed
phrases.notes: This is the Aramaic translation of ישעיהו 8:6, the verse about the waters of שילוח.

phrases.english: the kingdom of the house of David,
which leads them gently,
like the waters of the Shiloach, which flow gently,
and they took pleasure in Retzin and the son of Remalyahu."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִלְמָלֵא תַּרְגּוּמָא דְּהַאי קְרָא, לָא הֲוָה יָדַעְנָא מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of the ישעיהו verse quoted as רבשקה's source in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'waters of שילוח' stand for the gentle rule of בית דוד, which the people rejected in favor of רצין and בן רמליה.

steps.title: A cursed house and a blessed house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains a verse in משלי. The curse in the house of the wicked refers to פקח בן רמליהו, who ate huge amounts. The blessing on the home of the righteous refers to חזקיה, who ate very little and was satisfied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What does the verse mean, 'The curse of God is in the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous'? 'The curse of God is in the house of the wicked' means פקח בן רמליהו, who ate forty סאה of young birds for dessert. 'He blesses the home of the righteous' means חזקיה king of יהודה, who ate a ליטרא of vegetables at his meal.
steps.whatsHappening: Since בן רמליה was just mentioned, the גמרא brings a side teaching from רבי יוחנן. He contrasts the wicked פקח with the righteous חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'curse' is that פקח ate a massive amount and still did not feel satisfied. The 'blessing' is that חזקיה ate a tiny amount and was satisfied. This contrasts the wicked northern king the people preferred with a righteous king of בית דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Dessert, the end of the meal
A litra, a small measure of weight

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as praising someone for eating a lot. Eating forty סאה is the curse here, because his food never satisfied him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: What is the meaning of what is written:
"The curse of God is in the house of the wicked,
but He blesses the home of the righteous"?
"The curse of God is in the house of the wicked":
this is Pekach son of Remalyahu,
who would eat forty se'ah of young birds
for dessert.
"But He blesses the home of the righteous":
this is Chizkiyah, king of Judah,
who would eat a litra of vegetables at a meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching triggered by the mention of בן רמליה in the תרגום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The curse on the wicked is the never-satisfied eating of פקח; the blessing on the righteous is the small, satisfying meal of חזקיה.

steps.title: The rest of the prophecy: the king of אשור floods in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the prophecy. God will bring the king of אשור like a mighty river, and he will sweep through יהודה up to the neck. This is the source רבשקה pointed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Therefore, God is bringing upon them the mighty and abundant waters of the river, the king of Assyria.' And it is written: 'He will sweep through Judah, flood it and pass through, reaching up to the neck.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic and finishes quoting the prophecy that רבשקה relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the people rejected the gentle 'waters of שילוח,' God would send the strong 'waters of the river,' meaning the king of אשור. This is why רבשקה could claim that God sent him.

keyTerms.meaning: The waters of the river, a picture for the army of אשור

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the answer to רבי יהושע בן לוי's question in step 6, and it sets up the next question: if God sent him, why was he punished?

phrases.english: "Therefore, behold, God brings up upon them
the mighty and abundant waters of the river,
the king of Assyria,"
and it is written: "And he shall sweep through Judah,
he shall flood and pass through, he shall reach up to the neck."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָכֵן הִנֵּה ה׳ מַעֲלֶה עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת מֵי הַנָּהָר הָעֲצוּמִים וְהָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבי יוחנן's side teaching to finish quoting רבשקה's source.
steps.raayaObject: רבשקה's claim that God told him to go up against the land
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 8:7-8: God brings the king of אשור like a river over יהודה

steps.title: If God sent him, why was he punished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the prophecy shows that God sent סנחריב, why was he punished?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what is the reason he was punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. If סנחריב was carrying out God's plan, it seems unfair that he was punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 and 10 seemed to prove that God really did send the king of אשור. That makes his punishment in step 3, when the angel struck his camp, hard to understand.

phrases.english: But then, what is the reason he was punished?
phrases.notes: 'He' is סנחריב, whose camp was struck by the angel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of the previous steps: being sent by God seems to contradict being punished.
steps.kashyaTarget: The punishment of סנחריב described in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a prophecy said God would bring the king of אשור, he was doing God's will, so he should not deserve punishment.

steps.title: He went beyond what the prophecy allowed
steps.stepSummary: The prophecy was only about the ten tribes, but סנחריב set his sights on all of ירושלים. A prophet warned him with the verse 'there is no weariness to the one who oppresses her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The prophet prophesied about the ten tribes, but he set his mind on all of ירושלים. A prophet came and said to him: 'For there is no weariness for the one who oppresses her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סנחריב was punished because he went further than the prophecy allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God's permission covered the ten tribes of the northern kingdom. סנחריב also tried to conquer ירושלים, which was never part of the prophecy, so he was punished for that.

keyTerms.meaning: The ten tribes of the northern kingdom

steps.whatToRemember: Being God's tool for one task does not give permission to go further. סנחריב was punished for aiming at ירושלים, which the prophecy never included.

phrases.english: The prophet prophesied about the ten tribes,

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ יְהַיב דַּעְתֵּיהּ עַל כּוּלַּהּ יְרוּשָׁלֶם.
phrases.english: but he set his mind on all of Jerusalem.
A prophet came and said to him:
"For there is no weariness for the one who oppresses her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prophecy: the permission covered only the ten tribes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prophecy seemed to give סנחריב full permission, so his punishment looked unjustified.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was allowed to act only against the ten tribes; trying to take ירושלים went beyond that, so he was punished.

steps.title: A nation tired from תורה is not handed to its oppressor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר ברכיה reads the prophet's verse as a lesson: a nation that tires itself out with תורה is not handed over to the one who oppresses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר ברכיה said: A nation that is weary from תורה is not handed over to the one who oppresses it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בר ברכיה explains the verse the prophet said to סנחריב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads מועף as 'weary' and מוצק as 'oppressor.' The people of ירושלים in חזקיה's time worked hard at תורה, so they could not be given over to סנחריב. This explains why ירושלים was protected.
steps.whatToRemember: ירושלים was protected because its people were 'weary in תורה.' A nation that toils in תורה is not handed over to its oppressor.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Berechyah said:
A nation that is weary in Torah is not handed over
phrases.notes: 'Weary' (עייף) is a play on מועף in the verse, and 'oppresses' (מציק) on מוצק.

phrases.english: into the hand of the one who oppresses it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר בֶּרֶכְיָה: אֵין נִמְסָר עַם עָיֵיף בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse quoted by the prophet in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nation that toils in תורה is not handed over to its oppressor.

steps.title: The generation that made תורה heavy deserves a miracle
steps.stepSummary: The drasha continues with the next part of the verse in ישעיהו. The earlier generation lightened the yoke of תורה, but חזקיה's generation made it heavy, so they deserve a miracle like the sea and the Jordan. If סנחריב does not turn back, God will disgrace him among the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the verse mean: 'Now the former made it light, the land of זבולון and the land of נפתלי, but the latter made it heavy, by way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, the district of the nations'? It means: they are not like the earlier generation, who threw off the yoke of תורה. The later generation took the yoke of תורה heavily upon themselves. They deserve a miracle like the people who crossed the sea and walked through the Jordan. If סנחריב turns back, good. If not, I will make him rolled in shame among the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the prophet's verse as a lesson. It contrasts a generation that lightened its load of תורה with חזקיה's generation, which made that load heavy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the verse gets a new meaning. 'Made light' and 'made heavy' describe how seriously each generation took תורה. 'The sea' and 'the Jordan' point to the kind of miracle they deserve, and 'גליל הגוים' becomes סנחריב being 'rolled' (גליל) in disgrace. This builds directly on step 13: a people working hard in תורה is not handed over to its oppressor.

keyTerms.meaning: The yoke of תורה, the commitment to learn it and keep it
They made light, they threw off
They made heavy, they took it on seriously
Here it means rolled around, disgraced (a play on 'district')

phrases.english: What is the meaning of: "Now the former made it light
the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali
but the latter made it heavy, by way of the sea
beyond the Jordan, the district of the nations"?
Not like the earlier ones, who made light
the yoke of Torah from upon themselves
but the later ones, who made heavy
the yoke of Torah upon themselves
these are fit to have a miracle done for them
like those who crossed the sea and those who walked through the Jordan
If he turns back, good
phrases.notes: "He" is סנחריב. God is speaking about whether he will give up his plan.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – אֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה לוֹ גָּלִיל בַּגּוֹיִם
phrases.english: and if not, I will make him rolled in shame among the nations
phrases.notes: A play on the verse's word גליל, 'district', read as 'rolling around' in disgrace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the same prophecy from step 13 with its next verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה's generation, which made the yoke of תורה heavy, deserved a miracle like the splitting of the sea and the Jordan, and סנחריב would be disgraced if he did not turn back.

steps.title: Is an invasion the reward for חזקיה's faithfulness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the verse saying that 'after these matters and this truth' סנחריב invaded יהודה. It asks how an invasion could be the payback for חזקיה's loyal service.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'After these matters and this truth, סנחריב king of אשור came, entered יהודה, camped against the fortified cities, and planned to break into them.' Is this the gift given in return for that gift?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. The verse seems to say that right after חזקיה did good things, סנחריב attacked, and that looks like an unfair reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'after these matters and this truth' come right after the account of חזקיה's faithful service. Read simply, God's response to his devotion was an enemy invasion. The גמרא asks whether that can really be the 'gift' that matches חזקיה's 'gift'.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift, a present (here: the invasion)
A gift, a present (here: חזקיה's service)

phrases.english: "After these matters and this truth
Sennacherib king of Assyria came

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֹא בִיהוּדָה וַיִּחַן עַל הֶעָרִים הַבְּצֻרוֹת
phrases.english: and entered Judah and camped against the fortified cities
and planned to break into them for himself"
Is this gift the return for that gift?
phrases.notes: Both words mean 'gift'. The question is whether חזקיה's good deeds should be repaid with an attack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prophecy to the historical verse about the invasion and challenges what it seems to imply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain sense of the verse in דברי הימים, which puts סנחריב's invasion right after חזקיה's righteous acts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A righteous king should be rewarded, not attacked, so how can an invasion follow his devotion?

steps.title: God first swore to hand סנחריב over to חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that 'after the truth' means after God swore an oath. God knew that if He only promised חזקיה victory over סנחריב, חזקיה would refuse even the victory to avoid the fear, so God swore first.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'After the matters and the truth': after what? רבינא said: after הקדוש ברוך הוא acted first and swore. He said: If I tell חזקיה, 'I will bring סנחריב and hand him over into your hands,' he will say, 'I don't want him, and I don't want to be afraid of him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what 'truth' in the verse refers to: God's oath. The invasion was not a punishment. It was part of a planned victory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אמת' is read as a sworn promise. God wanted to give חזקיה the spoils of סנחריב's army, but knew חזקיה would turn down a victory that came with terror. So God locked in the plan with an oath before asking him. That makes the invasion the setup for a reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Jumped ahead, acted first before being asked
I will hand over into your hand

steps.confusionAlert: The verse's word 'האמת' (the truth) is not about חזקיה's honesty here. רבינא reads it as God's oath.

phrases.english: "After the matters and the truth": after what?
Ravina said

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שֶׁקָּפַץ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְנִשְׁבַּע
phrases.english: After the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted first and swore
And He said: If I tell Hezekiah
"I will bring Sennacherib
and hand him over into your hand"
right away he will say: I don't want him
and I don't want the fear of him

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַחֲרֵי הַדְּבָרִים וְהָאֱמֶת״, אַחַר מַאי? אָמַר רָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by reinterpreting 'האמת' in the verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The invasion came right after חזקיה's good deeds as a bad response to them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The invasion came after God's oath to deliver סנחריב into חזקיה's hands, so it was the start of a reward.

steps.title: The verse that records God's oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a verse from ישעיהו to show that God really did swear to break אשור in His land and remove its yoke from His people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted first and swore: 'I will bring him.' As it says: 'The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying: Surely as I planned, so it has happened, and as I decided, so it will stand: to break אשור in My land and trample him on My mountains. Then his yoke will be removed from them, and his burden will be removed from their shoulder.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבינא's claim that God swore an oath by quoting a verse that openly describes that oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said God 'swore'. This verse begins with 'נשבע ה׳ צבאות' and its subject is the breaking of אשור in the Land of Israel. That matches the oath to bring סנחריב and destroy him there.

keyTerms.meaning: I will trample him (related to אבוס, a feeding trough)

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד קָפַץ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְנִשְׁבַּע
phrases.english: Immediately the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted first and swore
that "I will bring him," as it is stated
"The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּמִּיתִי כֵּן הָיָתָה
phrases.english: Surely as I planned, so it has happened
and as I decided, so it will stand
to break Assyria in My land
and on My mountains trample him
then his yoke will be removed from them
and his burden will be removed from their shoulder"

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד קָפַץ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְנִשְׁבַּע: דְּמַיְיתֵינָא לֵיהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for the oath described in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that God swore ahead of time to bring סנחריב and destroy him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 14:24–25, 'נשבע ה׳ צבאות... לשבר אשור בארצי'.

steps.title: סנחריב's army becomes a feeding trough for חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the word 'אבוסנו' in the verse as 'אבוס', a feeding trough. סנחריב and his army would come and become a source of wealth for חזקיה and his people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Let סנחריב and his army come and become a feeding trough for חזקיה and his people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a reading of one word from the verse just quoted, explaining what the oath actually gave חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אבוסנו' sounds like 'אבוס', the trough animals eat from. So beyond defeating סנחריב, God meant for his army's riches to feed and support חזקיה's people. This finishes רבינא's point: the invasion was really a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A feeding trough, a source of food and wealth
His group, his followers or army

steps.whatToRemember: The invasion of סנחריב was not a punishment for חזקיה. God swore in advance to hand סנחריב over, and his army became a source of wealth for חזקיה's people, who had taken the yoke of תורה on themselves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said
Let Sennacherib and his army come
and become a feeding trough
phrases.notes: He is reading the verse's word אבוסנו as אבוס, a trough.

phrases.english: for Hezekiah and his people

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a key word of the verse quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב's army was meant to become a source of wealth, a 'feeding trough', for חזקיה and his people.

steps.title: The yoke breaks because of חזקיה's oil
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא reads 'שָׁמֶן' (fatness) in ישעיהו as 'שֶׁמֶן' (oil). סנחריב's yoke was broken because of the oil that burned in חזקיה's study halls.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says the yoke will be destroyed 'because of שמן.' רבי יצחק נפחא says: the yoke of סנחריב was destroyed because of חזקיה's oil, which burned in the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another verse about the fall of אשור and gives a drasha on one word in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse's word שמן is unclear. רבי יצחק נפחא reads it as oil, the oil of the lamps used for learning in חזקיה's time. So the victory over סנחריב came because of the תורה learned in that generation.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil (read from the verse's word שָׁמֶן, 'fatness')
The smith, a nickname of רבי יצחק

phrases.english: "And it shall come to pass on that day,
his burden shall be taken off your shoulder,
and his yoke off your neck,
and the yoke shall be destroyed because of fatness."
Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha says:
The yoke of Sennacherib was destroyed
because of the oil of Chizkiyahu,
phrases.notes: He reads the verse's word שָׁמֶן, 'fatness,' as שֶׁמֶן, 'oil.'

phrases.english: which would burn in the synagogues
and in the study halls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of drashot on ישעיהו about סנחריב's downfall, now linking it to the merit of Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב's yoke was broken in the merit of the oil burning for Torah study in חזקיה's time.

steps.title: חזקיה puts a sword at the study hall door
steps.stepSummary: To make sure everyone learned, חזקיה placed a sword at the entrance of the בית המדרש and warned that anyone not learning תורה would be stabbed with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did חזקיה do? He stuck a sword at the door of the בית המדרש and said: anyone who does not learn תורה will be stabbed with this sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how חזקיה got the whole nation to learn תורה, which is why so much oil burned in the study halls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the oil of learning brought the victory. This step shows how serious חזקיה was about תורה: he treated not learning as a deadly matter.

phrases.english: What did he do?

phrases.aramaic: נָעַץ חֶרֶב עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: He stuck a sword at the entrance of the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: and said: Anyone who does not engage in Torah
will be stabbed with this sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on step 19 by describing what חזקיה did to fill the study halls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה enforced Torah learning for the whole nation with a sword at the בית המדרש door.

steps.title: Even children knew the laws of purity
steps.stepSummary: The result of חזקיה's effort: across the whole land no ignorant person was found, and every man, woman, and child knew the laws of טומאה and טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They searched from דן to באר שבע and found no עם הארץ. From גבת to אנטיפרס they found no boy or girl, man or woman, who was not expert in the laws of טומאה and טהרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the amazing result of חזקיה's push for Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how deep the learning went: not only scholars, but even small children knew one of the hardest areas of הלכה. That is the level of learning that earned the miracle against סנחריב.

keyTerms.meaning: An ignorant person, someone without Torah knowledge
From דן to באר שבע, the whole land from north to south

phrases.english: They searched from Dan to Be'er Sheva,
and did not find an ignorant person.
From Gevat to Antipatris,
and they did not find a boy or a girl,
a man or a woman,
who were not experts
in the laws of impurity and purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of חזקיה's decree from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In חזקיה's generation everyone, even children, was expert in the laws of טומאה and טהרה.

steps.title: Verses describing that learning generation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings verses from ישעיהו about that generation: people lived simply with a few animals, and left valuable vineyards to grow thorns because they were busy with תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About that generation the verse says a man will raise just a young calf and two sheep. It also says places with a thousand vines worth a thousand silver coins will turn into briars and thorns. Even though the vines were so valuable, they were left for thorns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its description of חזקיה's generation with verses from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses describe people living on very little and letting rich fields go wild. The גמרא reads this as praise: they could have made a fortune farming, but they chose to spend their time learning תורה.
steps.confusionAlert: The thorns in the field are not a punishment here. The גמרא reads them as a sign of praise: the people left their fields because they were busy learning.

phrases.english: And about that generation it says:
"And it shall come to pass on that day
that a man shall raise a young calf
and two sheep, etc."
And it says:
"And it shall come to pass on that day, every place
where there were a thousand vines
worth a thousand silver coins
shall become briars and thorns."

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֶלֶף גֶּפֶן בְּאֶלֶף כָּסֶף,
phrases.english: Even though a thousand vines are worth a thousand silver coins,
it will be left for briars and thorns.
phrases.notes: The fields were worth a lot, but the people left them alone because they were busy learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings verses that describe the Torah-focused generation of step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that חזקיה's generation was fully devoted to Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 7:21 and 7:23, about simple living and valuable vineyards left to thorns.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה's generation was so devoted to Torah that everyone knew hard הלכות and they gave up great wealth to keep learning. This merit broke סנחריב's yoke.

steps.title: The prophet tells Israel to gather the spoils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a verse comparing the gathering of the spoils to locusts gathering, and says the prophet told Israel to gather the spoils of סנחריב's army.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Your spoils shall be gathered like the gathering of locusts.' The prophet said to Israel: gather your spoils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new drasha on a verse about the spoils from סנחריב's army. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the defeat of סנחריב's army, there was a huge amount of plunder. The prophet commands the people to collect it, which leads to the question of how it should be taken.

phrases.english: "And your spoils shall be gathered like the gathering of the locusts."
The prophet said to Israel:
Gather your spoils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the merit that won the war to what happened with the spoils afterward, connecting to step 18's idea that סנחריב's army became wealth for Israel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophet commanded Israel to gather the spoils of סנחריב's army.

steps.title: Grab for yourself or share?
steps.stepSummary: The people ask the prophet whether each person should take spoils for himself, or whether the spoils should be divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: should we each grab for ourselves, or should we divide it up?
steps.whatsHappening: The people ask a practical question about how to take the spoils. This sets up the prophet's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two options: each person keeps what he takes, or everything is collected and shared out, for example with the king. The people need to know which way is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: To plunder, each grabbing for himself

phrases.english: They said to him:
To plunder or to divide?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to carry out the command of step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the spoils are taken by each person for himself or divided among everyone.

steps.title: Like locusts: each one for himself
steps.stepSummary: The prophet answers using the verse: just as each locust gathers food for itself, each person takes spoils for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'like the gathering of the locusts.' Just as when locusts gather, each one takes for itself, so too with your spoils, each person takes for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The prophet answers the question from step 24 by explaining the comparison to locusts in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse's picture of locusts is the key. Locusts do not share; each one eats what it collects. So the spoils are not divided, and each person keeps what he takes.
steps.whatToRemember: The spoils of סנחריב's army were not shared out: like locusts, each person kept what he gathered.

phrases.english: He said to them: "Like the gathering of the locusts."
Just as in the gathering of the locusts,
each and every one is for itself,
so too your spoils:
each and every one for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each person takes spoils for himself, like locusts that each gather for themselves.

steps.title: Isn't some of the spoil stolen from the ten tribes?
steps.stepSummary: The people object that סנחריב's spoils include property of the עשרת השבטים, so taking it would be stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to the prophet: But isn't the property of the ten tribes mixed in with these spoils?
steps.whatsHappening: The people push back against the prophet's instruction to take the spoils. They worry that it includes Jewish property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנחריב had already conquered the northern kingdom before he came to ירושלים, so his army was carrying property that once belonged to Jews. Taking it could be גזל from fellow Jews. This challenges the permission given in step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: The ten tribes of the northern kingdom

phrases.english: They said to him:
But isn't the property of the ten tribes
mixed in with it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the spoils of סנחריב's army, which had already plundered the northern kingdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the prophet's permission (step 25) to take the spoils.
steps.kashyaTarget: The instruction that each person may take spoils for himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Part of the spoils is Jewish-owned property, so taking it would be stealing.

steps.title: Like pools that purify, the property is 'purified'
steps.stepSummary: The prophet reads גבים as pools of water: just as a מקוה purifies a person, Jewish property that falls to the nations becomes 'purified' and permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'As the rushing of גבים, he rushes upon it.' Just as these pools raise a person from טומאה to טהרה, so too Jewish property, once it falls into the hands of the nations, is immediately purified.
steps.whatsHappening: The prophet answers the worry by reading the same פסוק a second way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of the same פסוק. In its plain sense גבים means locusts, but the prophet reads it as pools of water, like a מקוה. 'Purified' here means the property is no longer considered stolen once the nations captured it, so Jews may take it.

keyTerms.meaning: Locusts; also read as pools of water

steps.confusionAlert: 'טיהר' here does not mean ritual purity of objects. It is a picture: the property is 'cleaned' of its stolen status.

phrases.english: He said to them:
"As the rushing of locusts, he rushes upon it."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:4. The word גבים can also mean pools of water, and the prophet plays on that.

phrases.english: Just as these pools
raise a person up
from impurity to purity,
so too the property of Israel,
once it falls into the hands of the nations of the world,
it is immediately purified.
phrases.notes: He means it's no longer treated as stolen, so it may be taken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּמַשַּׁק גֵּבִים שׁוֹקֵק בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק (locusts / pools) to show the property's status changed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spoils still belong to the ten tribes, so taking them is stealing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the nations captured it, the property lost its old status and may be taken.

steps.title: Support from רב פפא: Ammon and Moab purified through סיחון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the idea to רב פפא's rule that עמון and מואב's land became permitted after סיחון conquered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רב פפא's teaching, for רב פפא said: עמון and מואב were purified through סיחון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the prophet's answer with a similar rule from רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbade Israel to take the land of עמון and מואב. Once סיחון conquered it, the land became his, and Israel could take it from him. A conquest can change who owns something, and that is the same idea as in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with רב פפא's teaching
סיחון, the Emorite king who conquered part of Ammon and Moab

steps.whatToRemember: Conquest changes ownership. Jewish property captured by the nations is no longer treated as stolen, so Jews may take it, just as עמון ומואב טהרו בסיחון.

phrases.english: This is like Rav Pappa's teaching,
for Rav Pappa said:
Ammon and Moab were purified through Sichon.
phrases.notes: Israel couldn't take their land directly, but once סיחון conquered it, Israel could take it from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 27 with a parallel rule.
steps.raayaObject: That property captured by the nations loses its old status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב פפא: עמון ומואב טהרו בסיחון.

steps.title: רב הונא: סנחריב made ten journeys in one day
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says סנחריב traveled ten stages on that one day, and quotes the list of places in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: That wicked one made ten journeys on that day, as it says: 'He came to Aiath, passed Migron, left his baggage at Michmas. They crossed the pass, lodged at Geba; Ramah trembles, Gibeath Shaul flees. Cry out, daughter of Gallim; listen, Laish; poor Anathoth. Madmenah wanders, the people of Gebim flee. Today he will stand at Nov, and wave his hand at the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רב הונא describes how fast סנחריב marched toward ירושלים, using the פסוקים in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is a number: exactly ten journeys in one day. The proof is the list of places in the פסוק. That count is what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Ten journeys traveled
that wicked one on that day,
as it says:
"He came to Aiath, he passed through Migron,
at Michmas he leaves his baggage.
They crossed the pass; Geba is our lodging;
Ramah trembles; Gibeath Shaul has fled.
Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim;
listen, Laish; poor Anathoth.
Madmenah has wandered off;
the people of Gebim gather to flee.
This very day he will stand at Nov;
he will wave his hand at the mount of the daughter of Zion,
the hill of Jerusalem."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עֶשֶׂר מַסָּעוֹת נָסַע אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about סנחריב's march, after the spoils discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב traveled ten stages in a single day, as shown by the list of places in ישעיהו.

steps.title: But the verse lists more than ten places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק names more than ten places, so how can רב הונא say ten?
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are many more than ten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's count, because the list in the פסוק seems longer than ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every name in the פסוק counts as a stop, the total goes past ten. Either the number is wrong, or some names in the פסוק are not stops.

phrases.english: But these are many more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the number in רב הונא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim of exactly ten journeys.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק he cites names more than ten places.

steps.title: Some phrases are the prophet speaking to כנסת ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'בת גלים' and 'לישה' are not stops. They are the נביא encouraging כנסת ישראל and warning them about נבוכדנצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Cry out, daughter of Gallim': the prophet is saying to כנסת ישראל, 'Cry out, daughter of Gallim,' daughter of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, who did מצוות like the waves of the sea. 'Listen, Laish': Don't be afraid of this one. Be afraid of the wicked נבוכדנצר, who is compared to a lion, as it says: 'A lion has gone up from his thicket.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the count problem. Some of the words in the פסוק are messages, not places, so they drop out of the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גלים' is read as 'waves': the אבות did many מצוות, like waves. 'ליש' is read as 'lion', meaning נבוכדנצר, the real future danger, not סנחריב. Removing these phrases brings the count closer to ten. The next step begins explaining another phrase the same way, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation of Israel, the Jewish people as a whole

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא reads a פסוק: a word that looks like a place name can hide a message to the Jewish people.

phrases.english: "Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim" —
it is the prophet who says it
to the congregation of Israel:
"Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim,"
the daughter of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
who did מצוות like the waves of the sea.
phrases.notes: גלים means waves, so 'בת גלים' becomes 'daughter of the ones with waves of מצוות.'

phrases.english: "Listen, Laish" —
do not be afraid of this one,
rather, be afraid
of the wicked Nebuchadnezzar
who is compared to a lion,
phrases.notes: ליש is another word for lion, so 'לישה' hints at נבוכדנצר.

phrases.english: as it says: "A lion has gone up from his thicket, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: צַהֲלִי קוֹלֵךְ בַּת גַּלִּים – נָבִיא הוּא דְּקָאָמַר לַהּ לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting objection of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: some words in the פסוק are messages, not place names.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every name in the פסוק is a stop on סנחריב's march, giving more than ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בת גלים' and 'לישה' are the prophet speaking to כנסת ישראל, so they are not counted.

steps.title: Opening the next question about the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to ask about the meaning of the next phrase. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What...?
steps.whatsHappening: This one word sets up the next move: the גמרא is about to ask what the next phrase in the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening word 'מאי' appears here. The rest of the question, about the next words of the פסוק, continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: What...?
phrases.notes: The question continues on the next amud. It asks about the next words of the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the phrases of the פסוק, after 'בת גלים' and 'לישה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the next phrase in the פסוק (the question finishes on the next amud).
